items.text: **Consider life threatening causes of chest pain in all patients**
While assessing ABCs titrate oxygen, monitor vital signs and cardiac rhythm, start IV
Administer [[m:9050|aspirin]] if history suggests possible cardiac chest pain
Notify receiving facility immediately if [[p:3070|STEMI Alert]] criteria met
Place combination defibrillation/pacing pads on patient
Consider SL [[m:9220|nitroglycerin]] if suspected cardiac chest pain and no contraindication
An **EMT** may administer patient’s prescribed [[m:9220|nitroglycerin]], **Contact Hospital** for verbal order
For hypotension following [[m:9220|nitroglycerin]] give 250 ml NS bolus, reassess, and repeat bolus as needed. Do not give additional [[m:9220|nitroglycerin]].
Consider [[m:9230|opioid]] for chest pain refractory to [[m:9220|nitroglycerin]] if no contraindication
Consider repeat 12-lead if initial 12-lead non-diagnostic and/or patient’s condition changes
Consider additional 12-lead views such as R sided leads for R ventricular infarct if inferior MI present

sidebars.title: Life threatening causes of chest pain:

items.text: Suspected right ventricular ST-segment elevation MI (inferior STEMI pattern plus ST elevation in right-sided precordial leads e.g. V4R)
Recent use of erectile dysfunction (ED) medication (e.g. Viagra, Cialis)

sidebars.title: Causes of Chest Pain in Children:

items.text: Ischemia is rare but can be seen with a history of Kawasaki’s disease with coronary aneurysms
